newsitem.title: BOSNIA: First meeting of Bosnian presidency Monday-aide.
newsitem.headline: First meeting of Bosnian presidency Monday-aide.

text.p: The first meeting of Bosnia's newly-elected three-man collective presidency is likely to be held in Sarajevo on Monday, an adviser to current president Alija Izetbegovic, told Reuters on Thursday.
"We think the meeting will be held on Monday at the Konak house," said Mirsa Hajric, adviser to Izetbegovic.

Preliminary final results show Izetbegovic, a Moslem, topped the September 14 voting for the collective presidency and will serve as Chairman of the group for the next two years. Momcilo Krajisnik, a Serb, was placed second and Kresimir Zubak, a Croat, came in third.
"Mr Izetbegovic and Mr Zubak have both agreed to the date and place and Krajisnik is under terrific pressure from the American side to agree," Hajric said.

A spokesman for Carl Bildt, the international community's High Representative to Bosnia, cast doubt on Hajric's claim and said a variety of options as to when and where the three men would meet were still under active consideration.
"The report is premature," Colm Murphy, Bildt's spokesman, told reporters in Sarajevo.
Izetbegovic and Zubak have been nominal partners and allies in the Moslem-Croat federation currently headed by the Croat, which governs 51 per cent of Bosnia.
Krajisnik has been serving as speaker of the parliament of the Serb republic, which controls the other 49 per cent of Bosnia.
An avowed separatist, Krajisnik has been refusing to meet the other two members of the presidency in Sarajevo, a city which is under Moslem-Croat control.
Instead, Krajisnik suggested that a new building be erected on the boundary line between the Moslem-Croat federation and the Serb republic, with a door on Serb territory through which he could enter.

The Konak building where, according to Hajric, the first meeting of the new Presidency would be held, is an ornate 19th century structure where Josip Broz Tito often stayed when he ruled the former Yugoslavia.
The results of the September 14 election have yet to be certified by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which oversaw the polling.
A mandated appeals period is set to expire on Monday afternoon at the latest, which would clear the way for a presidency meeting.

The U.S. government is reported to be blocking a final lifting of sanctions against rump Yugoslavia and the Serb republic until they meet post-election obligations, including a successful meeting of the new Presidency.
